description: Tiny, hand-written knowledge base used by the laboratory's factuality and misinformation checkers. It is intentionally small and classroom-scale: it exists to make controlled test cases reproducible, not to be a real encyclopedia.

facts.text: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
The Earth orbits the Sun once every 365.25 days.
Humans have 46 chromosomes in each somatic cell.
Light travels through a vacuum at about 299792458 metres per second.
The Transformer architecture was introduced in the 2017 paper Attention Is All You Need.
Python is a general purpose programming language created by Guido van Rossum.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth.
Vaccines are tested in clinical trials before they are approved for public use.
Greenhouse gases trap heat in the Earth's atmosphere.
The human heart pumps blood through the circulatory system.
Temperature, top-k and top-p are decoding parameters of a language model.
Greedy decoding always selects the highest probability token.

false_claims.text: The Moon is made of cheese.
Humans only use ten percent of their brains.
The Great Wall of China is visible from the Moon with the naked eye.
Drinking water cures every known disease.
Goldfish have a memory of only three seconds.
Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
